findings.label: Build-scope test conflicts with origin/stack and both obvious resolutions are wrong
findings.detail: git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only HEAD origin/stack reports exactly one conflicted path: src/test/PillButtonBuildScope.test.ts. Upstream 1c847107 ('retire the two-tone button', owner instruction, landed 15:04:02, one minute after the branch commit) deleted the <span className="pill-label"> from both branches of PillButton and in the same commit narrowed that test's segment loop from [ 'pill-label', 'pill-action' ] to [ 'pill-action' ]. 47daedd9 rewrote the same regions to add the three-state skip gating and readPage(), keeping the two-segment loop. Resolving to the branch reinstates `expect( attrs.length, 'no element carries .pill-label in the built page' ).toBeGreaterThan( 0 )` against a component that cannot emit it, and CI runs that case rather than skipping it because build-test.yml builds before vitest. Resolving to upstream discards the finding-5 fix, and origin/stack still has the defect - `it( 'has a built page to inspect' )` is a plain it() asserting existsSync(PAGE), so npx vitest run with no out/ is red.
findings.action: Rebase the delta onto current origin/stack (tip 1c847107). Keep the branch's readPage() helper and the built = existsSync( OUT ) three-state gating; take upstream's [ 'pill-action' ] narrowing; update the third case's title and the docblock so neither claims two segments.

findings.label: Stale out/ is not distinguished from a current build
findings.detail: The gate is `const built = existsSync( OUT )`, which tests only that the directory exists. A leftover export from an earlier tree therefore runs every assertion against HTML that need not correspond to the current source, and the test passes or fails on the wrong artifact. The docblock documents three states (no out/, out/ without the page, page present) but not the stale-out/ state. This is the one failure mode that undermines a test whose entire value proposition is reading what the browser actually gets, and this workstream was already bitten by the same class of error when a Lambda was deployed from a 40-commit-stale tree.
findings.action: Compare a build marker or the page's mtime against the component sources, or at minimum record the stale-build hazard in the docblock alongside the three states already listed.

findings.label: The 2.5.3 property test's multi-segment ordering logic is now unexercised
findings.detail: src/test/PillButtonAccessibleName.test.tsx builds its segment list from the rendered DOM and asserts the accessible name contains every segment in reading order. All ten CALL_SITES still pass `label`, but after 1c847107 `label` is no longer rendered, so querySelectorAll('span') yields one segment at every call site and containsAllInOrder never evaluates an ordering. The test still passes and still catches an empty or disagreeing name, but the multi-segment half of the criterion it was written for has no coverage. Upstream-caused rather than this branch's, and defect 2's own coverage is unaffected - SignInMessages.test.tsx asserts .pill-label is null and .pill-action textContent is exactly 'Confirm code'.
findings.action: Either add a genuinely multi-segment fixture so the ordering path is exercised, or drop the inert `label` props from CALL_SITES and record in the docblock that a single-segment pill satisfies 2.5.3 trivially.

findings.label: No live OTP round trip
findings.detail: Both defects are verified in Chrome 154 over CDP against the real webpack export, but InitiateAuth, RespondToAuthChallenge and the session endpoint are all canned, so the deployed path has never been exercised end to end with a real WhatsApp code. The server fix is live (wecare-customer-session v5->v6, wecare-checkout v4->v5, wecare-wix-store v33->v34, recorded in a4144896), which makes the gap a confirmation gap rather than a correctness one. Correctly not attempted here: no live-send flag may be touched and a real code needs the owner's handset.
findings.action: Owner work. One handset sign-in on the QA recipient +918100640044 after the Amplify build carries the frontend commit, disambiguating the masked log suffix on direction, channel or the wecare-customer-whatsapp-auth delivery id.
